# Storm outlook for Punctual Pros

There is no storm this week in Punctual Pros' Pennsylvania hub markets. The forecast is dry and calm. The only active alert is a minor coastal flood advisory in south Jersey. The more relevant signal is cold nights near freezing at the start of heating season.

## Active alerts

- There is one alert across the eight states tracked. It is a Coastal Flood Advisory for New Jersey, rated "Minor" and "Likely" (National Weather Service alerts).
- It covers Ocean, Atlantic, Cape May and southeastern Burlington. It runs from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m. EDT on Oct 20, 2026.
- Atlantic County is listed as an "adjacent" territory tier (Punctual Pros storm events). The context does not show the tier for the other three counties.
- Pennsylvania has zero alerts.

## Hub forecast

All figures below come from the Open-Meteo forecast. Six of the ten hubs appear in the context.

- Gusts on Oct 20 peak around 24 mph at Lebanon. The windiest day was Oct 17, which has already passed, at 31.1 mph in Harrisburg.
- There is no rain or snow across the hubs shown.

## What it means for demand

- **Plumbing and electrical:** Storm-driven call spikes are unlikely this week (est.). There is no rain, wind event or outage alert in the Pennsylvania hubs.
- **HVAC:** Overnight lows of 33–35°F fall in October. October is the busiest HVAC month nationally because of heating start-up (Punctual Pros demand model, citing Samsara telematics). No-heat calls should be the main driver this week (est.).
- **Baseline:** The model uses 10 market-wide reactive HVAC calls per 10k households per day, with a range of 8–13 (Punctual Pros demand model).
- **Call volume:** A Punctual Pros call count cannot be produced from this context. Three inputs are missing:
  - county household counts;
  - the October monthly index;
  - Punctual Pros market share, which the model lists as an unknown parameter.
- **Model status:** Heating multipliers are still assumptions. They are not yet calibrated to Punctual Pros data.

## Next actions

1. Pull October-to-date booked calls by trade from ServiceTitan. Compare them with prior Octobers to size the heating start-up surge.
2. Confirm technician and dispatch coverage for no-heat calls on cold mornings. Off-hours inbound calls peak from 5 to 9 p.m. local (Punctual Pros demand model).
3. Confirm whether Ocean, Cape May and Burlington are served or adjacent territory. Then judge whether the Oct 20 advisory matters operationally.
4. Load 12+ months of Punctual Pros call history so the weather multipliers can be fitted and the market-share parameter set.
